submission.justification: Radiator-R3 gives the best separation (4.56 sigma at 3 cm), but I found no humidity-ageing data for any candidate. R3 is a high-index porous radiator with no mentioned hydrophobic treatment, so it is the one most likely to fail the hard 10% transparency limit. R1 is porous with a hydrophobic treatment and gives 3.89 sigma at 3 cm, which is its best thickness in my scan. I recommend it as the best option that plausibly meets the hard constraint. The humidity result for R1 is NOT verified. A 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must be run on R1 before procurement. If R1 fails, R2 is the fallback, and R3 would be the choice only if it passes the test. The dry nitrogen flush in the vessel is not evidence of ageing performance.

requirements.requirement: Best possible pi/K separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R3 is best at 4.56 sigma at 3 cm. R1 at 3 cm gives 3.89 sigma, so the recommendation gives up some separation. R1 scan: 2 cm 3.63, 3 cm 3.89, 4 cm 3.51, 6 cm 2.74 sigma. R3 scan: 2 cm 4.48, 3 cm 4.56, 4 cm 4.19, 6 cm 3.27 sigma.
No document gives humidity-ageing results for any candidate. R1's hydrophobic treatment suggests it may pass, but this is not measured.

requirements.requirement: Radiator is one of the three candidates
